newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FERC urged to reject PECO power pool plan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FERC urged to reject PECO power pool plan.

text.p: Seven utilities of the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Power Pool filed a motion asking the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to reject PECO Energy Co's plan to restructure the pool.

The seven big utilities of the power pool, called the Supporting Companies, in a statement said the PECO proposal would deny other pool members the economic and reliability benefits of power pooling and was inconsistent with FERC's efforts to encourage power pooling.
PECO, backed by power marketers, filed its pool restructuring proposal June 9, while the Supporting Companies filed another proposal June 2.

The utilities said PECO proposed a "vague" transition plan that "would do away with the core functions of the PJM pool -- eliminating an efficient interchange energy market, reserve sharing and coordination with neighboring pools -- and leave only a for-profit, regional transmission operator in its place."
